paper.title: Properties of Fe–Mn–Al alloys with different Mn contents using density functional theory
paper.paper_scope: First-principles DFT study of the chemical stability, electronic structures, mechanical/elastic properties, mechanical anisotropy and Debye temperature of B2-type Fe1-xMnxAl alloys (x = 0 to 1) with different Mn contents.

alloys.description: Mn-free end member (x = 0) of the Fe1-xMnxAl series; B2-type cubic Fe-Al parent compound (space group Pm-3m) from which other structures are derived by substituting Fe with Mn.

processes.description: Geometry-optimized crystal structure via first-principles DFT using CASTEP; GGA-PBE exchange-correlation, ultrasoft pseudopotentials, 8x8x8 Monkhorst-Pack k-point mesh, 450 eV plane-wave cutoff, energy converged to 2x10^-6 eV and forces below 0.5 eV/nm.
processes.processes_notes: Computational study with no experimental thermal/mechanical processing. The same DFT optimization/calculation protocol was applied to all Fe1-xMnxAl alloys, so it does not by itself distinguish the samples (the Mn content does).

source.reason: The only process/state identity is the DFT first-principles calculation protocol described in the Calculation methods section, applied uniformly to all Fe1-xMnxAl crystal structures.

unmapped_findings: Pure Fe, Mn and Al appear in Table 1 only as reference states for calculating cohesive energy and formation enthalpy; they are not among the studied Fe–Mn–Al alloy objects.

Key paper-level results: FeAl is the most thermodynamically stable (lowest formation enthalpy, -0.391 eV/atom) and has the highest bulk/shear/Young's moduli (187.1/119.8/296.2 GPa), highest hardness (16.5 GPa) and highest Debye temperature (652.5 K); MnAl has the strongest elastic anisotropy (A^U = 3.80) and the lowest Debye temperature (504.1 K).
